Thanks again for taking the demo today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the POC: 

Highlights from the call:
- Goal: Reduce time-to-insight for support agents by surfacing grounded answers from product docs and knowledge base.
- Top concerns you raised: hallucination with long-tail queries, latency under 300ms 95p for agent UI, and indexing cadence for frequently changing KBs.

Recommended evaluation approach (short):
1) Models to try: redwood-instruct-3b (fast, quant-friendly) + redwood-rlhf-7b (higher-quality for nuanced grounding). As a fallback, opt-13b-4bit for heavier context needs.
2) Retrieval config: dense embeddings (512-d, cosine) + BM25 hybrid. Suggest initial settings: embed top_k=10, bm25 top_k=100, hybrid scoring weight=0.6 (embed)/0.4 (bm25).
3) Reranker: cross-encoder reranker (distilroberta-cross-encoder fine-tuned on QA pairs) to improve precision@1.
4) Grounding metrics: precision@1, grounding rate (fraction of answers with at least one citation), and answer acceptance rate from agent feedback. Track hallucination rate via manual spot checks.

Attachments I’m sharing: acme-rag-prompt-set.csv (sample prompts + expected output schema), rag-bench-summary.pdf (short bench vs. our models), acme-eval-sample.jsonl (sample eval set). Links to the benchmark dashboard and the prompt set are below.

Proposed next steps:
- Your team: confirm a 2-week POC window and preferred KB snapshot date.
- Ours: spin up a dedicated eval harness, run the two model configs, and return bench + prompt-by-prompt failures.
- Set a 30-min sync for early next week to review results (I can do Tue/Wed morning PT).

Let me know if you want me to include a pricing outline for a short Dedicated GPU trial for the POC — I can loop in Aditya.

Thanks Sofia — answers below inline.

On 10/12/26 5:08 PM, Sofia Morales wrote:
> 1) Grounding / hallucination: can you share how you define "grounding rate" operationally?

We define grounding rate as: the fraction of returned answers (top-1) that include at least one explicit citation to a source document (doc id + snippet). For evaluation we count a citation as valid if the quoted snippet overlaps >=50% token overlap with the labeled supporting span in the gold set. That gives you a conservative grounding metric and helps measure partial matches separately.

> 2) Reranker latency: the cross-encoder approach sounds right for precision but worried about end-to-end latency. Do you have numbers for a 7b cross-encoder + redwood-rlhf-7b setup?

Short answers:
- With batched cross-encoder reranking (batch size 16) we see ~40-80ms per query for the reranker on a modern GPU; end-to-end 95p latency to first token for the generator with reranker in the loop typically sits ~180-320ms depending on sequence length and batch overlap.
- If 95p <300ms is a hard SLO we can: (a) reduce cross-encoder batches, (b) use a smaller distilled cross-encoder as a first-pass, or (c) limit reranker candidates to top_k=10. I’ll include two config options in the eval run.

> 3) KB cadence / connectors

For hourly updates we recommend incremental indexing using a lightweight change-log processor (we have a connector pattern for S3 -> incremental vector upserts + ES for BM25). This avoids full rebuilds; we sync deltas every 10-15m in the POC. We’ll share the connector template and the expected IAM role/permissions needed.

Next steps: we’ll schedule a 30-min sync on Tue 10/20 at 9:00 AM PT if that works for your team — I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm. I’ve also uploaded a short bench report and the prompt set to the Drive folder linked below.
